method: rates by number of deaths on matched exposure; nothing pooled across datasets
primary_basis: Singapore: fatal fires in premises counted in the dwelling stock, 2012-2025; England: dwelling fires, 2012/13 to 2025/26

capture_bounds.note: upper bounds on the Singapore fatal dwelling-fire rate: every death in the official series (any type of fire), or every death in the register including boundary events, taken as a separate single-death dwelling fire

england_strictest_definition.note: England restricted to accidental dwelling fires and to deaths at the scene with a recorded fire cause; Singapore unrestricted

two_processes_england_dwellings.note: one row per death; the 71 Grenfell Tower records are set aside

position_checks.note: position when the fire started; 'elsewhere' is a different floor, room, cabin or compartment from the fire origin; every victim stays in the denominator

fires_with_exactly_two_deaths.note: rebuilt by grouping, so conditional on the grouping; every fire has the same weight

deaths_in_multiple_death_fires.note: deaths in one fire are not independent, so no interval is given
deaths in one fire are not independent, so no interval is given

household_standardisation.source: Home Office (2022) in-depth review, Table 38; fatal dwelling fires 2010/11 to 2018/19
household_standardisation.note: English rates are for 2010/11 to 2018/19 and are applied to Singapore resident households of 2012 to 2025

Singapore, dwelling stock.label: Singapore 2012-2025, premises in the dwelling stock

United States, residential buildings.label: United States 2021-2023, residential buildings, shares among reported fires
United States, residential buildings.note: published percentage (76.8% two deaths, 14.3% three, 4.7% four, 4.2% five or more); counts not published

Australia_preventable_residential.label: Australia FY2003/04 to 2016/17, residential, intent excluded

singapore_tail_with_english_shape.note: Singapore's own rate of multiple-death building fires with the shape of English dwelling fires above one death

United States.scope_of_source: residential buildings, all causes, 2018-2020; scaled national estimate

second_period_2021_2023.note: direct national estimate of 200 multiple-death fires a year, published rounded to the nearest 100, stated as 11% of fatal fires

all_allowances_compounded.note: household and age standardisation multiplied by the effect of the strictest English definition (accidental fires, deaths at the scene, recorded cause) applied to England alone; an upper bound on the single-death ratio, since the definition is not applied to Singapore

separation_after_allowances.note: ratio of the multiple-death rate ratio to the single-death rate ratio (Equation 8) after each allowance; exact interval and central p conditional on Singapore's total, with the English expectations taken as fixed

compounded_with_english_count_error.note: 2.5, 50 and 97.5 percentiles; all counts drawn, exposures fixed; an approximate check on the exact intervals, which carry Singapore's count error only

capture_tipping.note: capture of single-death fires relative to multiple-death fires, as a fraction of England's, that would alone produce the crude separation of the two rate ratios; and the unrecorded single-death fires that would bring Singapore's share down to England's

model_free_tail.note: the likelihood of a record with no fire above four deaths is multiplied by (1 - eps)^K when probability eps is moved above four deaths, wherever it is placed

england_bounds_from_official_counts.note: sharp bounds for each threshold separately; one allocation need not attain them at every threshold together. Grenfell Tower is included in the counts of 2017/18.

known_answer_test.note: English dwelling fires, Grenfell Tower set aside; fires expected at 3, 4 and 5 or more deaths under a single power law fitted to all fatal fires and under the three-part form; 'chance' is the Poisson probability of a count at least as far from the expectation as the nearer official bound

edition_note.note: the household rows take single-death fires from the review table; both totals include Grenfell Tower
